audit.whatIsWrong: win[5] and win[6] read Darius while whys[5] says 'First item her vitals true damage and Riposte flip it to Fiora' and whys[6] says 'With two-plus items her dueling, mobility and parry beat you.' spikes[2].text, spikes[3].text, mid and late all say the same. Two rows contradict their own verdicts.
audit.why: The packet levelChart independently records Fiora at first item and two-plus items, and no fiora__darius mirror file exists to pin them the other way. The 54.9% win rate over 2694 games is not in conflict with this: Darius wins the lane phase outright and Fiora out-scales it, which is exactly the shape the prose already describes. I flipped only those two rows plus their ratings, as one atomic group.
audit.corrected: First item and two-plus items belong to Fiora; levels 1-5 stay Darius.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why is the generic Noxian Guillotine boilerplate and carries an un-rendered formula, 'R = d + a \times Stacks'. Grand Challenge lands on the same level and is never mentioned. phases[5].why credits the stage to Stridebreaker on a row that actually belongs to Fiora.
audit.why: Grand Challenge is 110/90/70 seconds at 500 range and 'reveals all four Vitals on an enemy champion... If Fiora hits all four Vitals or if the target dies after she has hit at least one, Fiora and her allies in the area are healed.' The heal triggering on the target's death after a single Vital is the part that matters: dying to a Fiora who is behind still hands her side a heal, so a failed all-in is worse than no all-in. Lunge is 13 seconds at rank 1 and only 6 at rank 5, so her mobility roughly doubles across the item stages while Apprehend stays at 26 down to 16.
audit.corrected: Grand Challenge is 110s at rank 1 and reveals all four Vitals. Hitting all four, or killing you after even one, heals Fiora and every ally standing near her.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page states in four places that Riposte parries and then stuns - spikes[1].text ('your stun window flips on you'), spikes[2].text ('Riposte parries your Q and stuns you'), mid ('Riposte can parry-stun your committed Q'), dosFull[0].d and report[5].t ('Parries your pull + stuns'). Riot's own text makes the stun conditional and the page drops the condition entirely. The tldr also tells the player to 'flatly hug terrain walls to block her ultimate', which no property of Grand Challenge supports.
audit.why: Riposte (W, 24/22/20/18/16s, 750 range): 'Fiora parries all incoming damage and disables for a short time, then stabs in a direction. This stab slows the first enemy champion hit, or stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with this ability.' The default outcome is a slow. The stun is an upgrade she only gets by parrying an immobilizing effect, so a Riposte that eats Decimate leaves you slowed, not stunned - a materially different thing to plan a commit around. Grand Challenge is a 500-range reveal on a champion; terrain does not interact with it. Bladework (E, 11/10/9/8/7s) gives 'increased attack speed for the next two attacks. The first attack slows the target, and the second attack will critically strike' - a guaranteed crit on a known beat, which is the burst tell the page never gives.
audit.corrected: Riposte's stab only stuns if it parried an immobilizing effect; on Decimate it is a slow. Bladework's second attack is a guaranteed critical strike.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Riposte and gives no number, then runs into two paragraphs of leaked source prose about Apprehend and Ghost that are not cooldowns at all.
audit.why: Riposte 24/22/20/18/16 is the single longest non-ultimate cooldown Fiora has and is very close to Apprehend's 26/23.5/21/18.5/16, so the lane is genuinely two long cooldowns staring at each other. Lunge 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6, Bladework 11/10/9/8/7, Grand Challenge 110/90/70.
audit.corrected: Riposte 24s at rank 1, Lunge 13s at rank 1 down to 6s, Bladework 11s, Grand Challenge 110s.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.early says 'Anti-heal her late sustain' without naming what heals her.
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/_missing/darius.json flags Duelist's Dance and Grand Challenge as the anti-heal targets in this matchup. Duelist's Dance restores health on every Vital hit, so the sustain is not late at all - it is running from level 1, which changes when Grievous Wounds is worth buying.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal her Vital sustain, which is live from level 1, not just her ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fiora is called 'he' or 'his' in tradeGood, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[0].d and breakdown.mid.
audit.why: Fiora is female throughout Riot's text ('If she hits the Vital, she restores Health').

notes: UNVERIFIED, and the reason I phrased every Riposte edit around 'an immobilizing effect' rather than around your pull: whether Apprehend counts as an immobilizing effect for Riposte's stun upgrade is not answerable from the kits, and it is the same open question that sits on Dr. Mundo's passive. Riot's Riposte text gives the condition without defining the category, and Apprehend is described only as a hook that pulls enemies to him. So the page now states the rule exactly as Riot states it and lets the player apply it, rather than asserting that a pull does or does not trigger the stun. I also left breakdown.early's older phrasing about the parry catching the pull out of the rewrite for the same reason. Separately: diff reads FAV while diffRating is 8/10 and both breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t say 'Hard matchup'. Darius wins this 54.9%. I did not touch it because with first item and two-plus items now correctly flipped to Fiora, 'hard but favoured' is defensible - but the label and the rating should be reconciled deliberately rather than by me guessing. Also note breakdown.wave and report[4].t carry the same leaked source block seen on camille, chogath and drmundo.
